body:
STORYATLAS PIN AUDIT — current evidence, no claim or edit.

Measured at StoryAtlas 003f12b and storymodel4s 99dc378. build.sbt still pins storymodel4s 3cf704a. Live origin/main is exactly 7385cf9379e59599d1e18370049ac73782844816, so the consumer pin is now 137 commits behind the published dependency and 205 behind local main.

Source compatibility is encouraging but not a gate. Across 3cf704a..7385cf9, the entire view directory is byte-unchanged. The only production WarOfTheGhostsModel change moves four private ID helper definitions to file scope to eliminate an initialization-order cycle; the public model source and values are otherwise unchanged. The published range changes 39 files overall, chiefly core/features/codec contracts and tests. Across 7385cf9..local HEAD, production view and fixture sources remain unchanged; local-only production changes are in align, codec-align, embed-bench/onnx, and interview.

I attempted a clean no-edit compatibility probe against an exact detached 7385cf9 source clone. It loaded StoryAtlas, storymodel4s, grakern, and gale, then failed during dependency resolution with java.io.IOException: No space left on device. That is infrastructure-inconclusive, not a compatibility failure. The volume had 120 MiB free. I removed only my reproducible /tmp audit directory (393 MiB), restoring 522 MiB; no repository or other session artifact was deleted.

Required next court remains the bead's existing contract: choose one published target, edit the real StoryAtlas pin, run without local override, prove exact revision in receipts, run compileAll/testAll/scalafmt and browser semantic-selection courts, and compare old/new WOG artifacts across zoom/lens/horizon. Any scientific byte delta becomes a provider-contract migration, not a routine bump.

Chief decision requested: target currently published 7385cf9 now, or wait for the 68 local commits to be reviewed and published and bump once. I recommend 7385cf9 now because the consumer is already 137 published commits stale, but I will not claim or edit until the target and exact paths are assigned.
